original_value: Multi-label learning has become an important area of research owing to the increasing number of real-world problems that contain multi-label data. Data labeling is an expensive process that requires expert handling. The annotation of multi-label data is laborious since a human expert needs to consider the presence/absence of each possible label. Consequently, numerous modern multi-label problems may involve a small number of labeled examples and plentiful unlabeled examples simultaneously. Active learning methods allow us to induce better classifiers by selecting the most useful unlabeled data, thus considerably reducing the labeling effort and the cost of training an accurate model. Batch-mode active learning methods focus on selecting a set of unlabeled examples in each iteration in such a way that the selected examples are informative and as diverse as possible. This article presents a strategy to perform batch-mode active learning on multi-label data. The batch-mode active learning is formulated as a multi-objective problem, and it is solved by means of an evolutionary algorithm. Extensive experiments were conducted in a large collection of datasets, and the experimental results confirmed the effectiveness of our proposal for better batch-mode multi-label active learning.

result.paraphrase: Multi-label learning has become an important research area due to the growing number of real-world problems involving multi-label data. Labeling data is costly and requires expert intervention. Annotating multi-label data is labor-intensive because a human expert must assess the presence or absence of every possible label. As a result, many contemporary multi-label problems have only a small number of labeled examples while also containing many unlabeled ones. Active learning methods can improve classifiers by choosing the most useful unlabeled data, thereby greatly reducing labeling effort and the expense of training an accurate model. Batch-mode active learning methods aim to select, at each iteration, a set of unlabeled examples that is both informative and as diverse as possible. This article proposes a strategy for batch-mode active learning on multi-label data. The method is framed as a multi-objective problem and solved using an evolutionary algorithm. Extensive experiments were carried out on a large set of datasets, and the results confirmed the effectiveness of our proposal for improved batch-mode multi-label active learning.
